title: Literature check: pcell-mwall's catalyst selection is a variant of Ono & Ikegami 2002, active-nematic division plus motility is known (Giomi & DeSimone 2014), Particle Lenia rings look new; untried: lattice protocells, boundary-driven droplets, multistable autocatalytic kinds
summary: First literature check in the collective. Nearest prior art: Ono & Ikegami (ALIFE8 2002) report selection, through cellular reproduction, of catalysts with higher membrane-chemical production in lattice protocells that form from random soup, so c14's pcell-mwall is a variant (the identical-event marker and intrinsic deaths are the additions). Giomi & DeSimone (PRL 2014) already show division and motility of active nematic droplets, so c11/c15's rods are a variant; their self-made rings are new. Evoloop is Sayama 1999. Particle Lenia rings and their fission-fusion look new. Untried operators for open challenges: Ono-Ikegami lattice protocells with membrane renewal (IBED with turnover), boundary-driven active droplets (Bauermann et al. 2022), and multistable autocatalytic networks for discrete heritable kinds (Matsubara et al.). Two questions follow.
